phases.name: Spec, tracker, CI workers, session protocol
Engine core, inspection, encryption, repair, CLI
Organize, page design, annotate, document structure

features.name: Specification document (SPEC.md) with generated feature catalog
Live feature tracker (React JSX) driven by features.json
Token-free review workers (lint, types, tests, security, tracker gate), run locally
Evidence gate: a feature is done only when its linked tests pass
Golden PDF test corpus generator (fonts, encryption, forms, scans, broken files)
Automatic resume after a session ends abruptly (in-progress mark, recovery report)
Render pages to raster at any DPI
Document inspection report (version, fonts, images, encryption, forms, signatures, layers)
Typed, serializable operation (Op) model with JSON schema
Full rewrite save with garbage collection
Never overwrite the original by default (versioned outputs)
Large-document handling (1,000+ pages, lazy page loading)
Open encrypted PDFs with user password (RC4 40/128, AES-128, AES-256 R5/R6)
Open owner-restricted PDFs and report permission flags
Save edits while preserving the original encryption settings
Protect: add password with AES-256 encryption
criteria: Adding a password with no existing encryption produces a file that pikepdf/PyMuPDF refuse to open without the password
Both a user (open) and an owner (permissions) password can be set, and they differ
The file is encrypted with AES-256 (R6), never RC4 or 40/128-bit RC4
The original is never overwritten in place without the owner's confirmation; a save-as path is always available

features.name: Unlock: remove encryption when the valid password is supplied
criteria: Supplying the correct user or owner password removes encryption and the saved file opens with no password
An incorrect password is refused with a clear error, and the file is left untouched
Removing encryption preserves content, bookmarks, forms and signatures byte-for-byte where unrelated to encryption

features.name: Set document permissions (print, copy, modify, annotate)
criteria: Each of print, copy (extraction), modify and annotate can be independently allowed or denied
Denying a permission is reflected in the saved file's permission bits and in PDFWorkerz's own inspection report
Setting permissions without a user password still requires an owner password, so the restriction cannot be bypassed by opening with no password

features.name: True redaction (removes text, images and vectors under the mark)
criteria: Marking a rectangular area for redaction and applying it removes the underlying text's glyphs, any image pixels and any vector paths inside the area, not just drawing a black box over them
After saving, the content stream itself contains no operators that would redraw the removed content (not merely hidden by a later layer)
A redaction area that partially overlaps a text span removes only the covered glyphs, leaving the rest of the span exactly in place (reusing the existing per-glyph redaction primitives)
Redacting one area never alters pixels outside it on the same page

features.name: Redaction pattern packs (email, phone, SSN, card numbers, custom regex)
criteria: Built-in patterns for email, phone, US SSN and credit-card numbers find true matches across a mixed sample page and are regex-driven, so a user can verify the pattern used
A custom regex pattern can be supplied and runs the same way
Running a pattern pack produces a reviewable list of proposed redaction areas before anything is removed; nothing is redacted without confirmation
Accepting the list applies true redaction (SEC-08) to every matched area in one undo step

features.name: Sanitize: remove metadata, XMP, JavaScript, embedded files, hidden text
criteria: Sanitizing removes document metadata (Info dictionary) and XMP metadata
Sanitizing removes embedded JavaScript (document-level and field-level) so no /JS or /JavaScript actions remain
Sanitizing removes embedded files (attachments) from the saved file
Sanitizing removes or flattens hidden text (PDF render mode 3 / invisible OCR text layers) so nothing invisible remains extractable, while visible content is unaffected
The operation reports what it removed, and each category can be opted out individually

features.name: Redaction verification (re-extract after save proves removal)
criteria: After a redaction is saved, re-opening the file and extracting text/images from the redacted area finds nothing of the original content
Verification runs automatically after every redacting save and raises a clear failure (not a silent success) if anything redacted is still extractable
Verification also checks the page's raw content stream and resources, not only the high-level text/image extraction APIs, so content hidden via an unreferenced XObject is also caught

features.name: Per-span style extraction (font, size, color, flags, origin, bbox)
Per-character trace (char/word spacing, scaling, rise, render mode, opacity, matrix)
Font classification (type, embedding, subset tag, encoding, ToUnicode)
Subset glyph-coverage check for replacement text
Full-font lookup (system fonts + bundled OFL library, name normalization)
Metric-similarity font matching with confidence score
Glyph-borrow merge into the embedded subset font
Fit-to-width (tracking or horizontal scaling within tolerance)
Paragraph reflow within its own lines, keeping the baseline
Pixel-verified edit (before/after region diff with mismatch flag)
Type3 font handling (detect, reuse glyph procedures or fall back)
Scanned-text style estimation (font class, size, color)
Justified reflow, and moving later content when a paragraph grows
Per-character spacing kept through a text-only edit (TJ kerning, spacing that changes mid-line)
Icons and emoji recognised as their own units (Type3, PUA, emoji ranges), never edited away by a nearby restyle, insert, move or re-wrap
Move, copy and shift icons and emoji by re-using the document's own glyph drawing (incl. Type3)
Inline text edit that matches the original style
Find and replace (literal, regex, whole word, case sensitive)
Add new text with 'match style of' or explicit style
Change font, size, color and weight of existing text
Format painter (copy style from one span to another)
Insert, replace, resize, crop and delete images
Draw and edit vector shapes and lines
Edit text on scanned pages (OCR + background patch reconstruction)
Select several objects (Shift+click, marquee); align and distribute text blocks, images and shapes
Smart guides that snap dragged objects to other objects and the page; arrow-key nudging
Copy, paste, duplicate and delete page objects (text blocks, images, shapes), across pages
Select text by block, line or word (Nitro-style selection mode)
criteria: Lines are grouped deterministically from glyphs: mixed-style runs, superscripts, two columns, rotated text and fit-fragmented spans
Words are split from glyphs: across spans, spaces made by TJ gaps, punctuation kept with its word
GET .../pages/{p}/text_units?granularity=block|line|word serves the frozen TextUnit contract
The toolbar toggles Block / Line / Word (B/L/W keys), defaults to Line and remembers the choice
The inspector shows the selected unit's text and marks style fields that differ across it as mixed

features.name: Edit and restyle a single line or word in place
criteria: A same-width word edit leaves every other glyph pixel-identical; a wider or narrower one shifts only the rest of that line
Restyling a word leaves the glyphs before it unmoved and shifts the rest of its line only by the change in its width (nothing moves for a colour change)
Editing a line keeps the styles of the runs whose text did not change
Editing or restyling a block goes through index-addressed reflow
In the UI, Enter commits a unit edit as one undo step and reselects the edited unit

features.name: Move, nudge, align, copy, paste, duplicate and delete single lines and words
criteria: Moving a word leaves the rest of its line pixel-identical
Moving a line leaves the rest of its block in place
Duplicating a line or word works on the same page and onto another page
Deleting a word removes one adjacent space and closes the gap according to the line's alignment
A selection mixing blocks, lines and words is one undo step, drops units contained in other selected units, and survives span renumbering
In the UI, drag, nudge, align, Ctrl+C/V/D and Delete work in Line and Word modes

features.name: Line-aware text blocks: paragraphs stay whole after in-line edits
criteria: After a word edit splits a line into several spans, Block mode still selects the whole paragraph
Moving or copying a block keeps each run's own font, size and color

features.name: Insert copied lines or rows into a block, optionally pushing the existing lines down
Click-to-edit overlay styled with the detected font
Inspector panel (detected font, size, color, spacing, confidence)
Several documents open at once (tabs), copy and paste between them, apply an edit or recipe to all open
Expandable inspector panel (resizable, collapsible sections, larger text editor)
Target selectors ("text", /regex/, page ranges, odd/even, all pages)
Style modifiers (match style, bold, size, color)
'Did you mean' suggestions; never guesses silently
Recipes: save history as YAML/JSON and replay
Split (ranges, every N pages, by size, by bookmarks)
Extract pages to a new file
Insert blank pages or pages from another file
Page numbers (position, format, start value, skip pages)
Text and image watermarks (opacity, rotation, behind/over content)
Shape, line, arrow and freehand annotations
Edit metadata (title, author, subject, keywords, XMP)
Auto-generate bookmarks and TOC from heading styles
Detect and list AcroForm fields
criteria: Every AcroForm field on a page is listed with its type (text, checkbox, radio, dropdown, listbox, signature), name, rectangle and current value
Fields that share one field name (radio groups) are reported as one logical field with its options
A document with no AcroForm reports an empty list, not an error

features.name: Fill form fields
criteria: Setting a text field's value updates its appearance stream so the new value renders without needing a PDF viewer to regenerate it
Checking/unchecking a checkbox and choosing a radio option or dropdown value updates the field and its appearance correctly
Filling an unknown field name is refused with a clear error rather than silently doing nothing
Filling is one undoable Op, and filling several fields in one call is one undo step

features.name: Create and edit fields (text, checkbox, radio, dropdown, signature)
criteria: A text, checkbox, radio, dropdown and signature field can each be created at a given page position with a given name
An existing field's type-specific properties (e.g. a dropdown's options, a text field's font/size/multiline flag) can be edited after creation
A created field appears in FRM-01's listing and can be filled by FRM-02
Deleting a field removes it from the page's annotations and the AcroForm's field tree

features.name: Auto-detect fields on flat forms (lines, boxes, labels)
criteria: Given a flat (non-interactive) form page image, horizontal lines/underscores and rectangular boxes near a text label are detected as likely field locations

Each detected location is turned into a proposed field (text field for a line, checkbox for a small box) with a position and a best-guess name from the nearby label, shown for review before anything is created
Accepting the proposals creates real AcroForm fields (via FRM-03) in one undo step; nothing is created without confirmation
A page with no visual form cues yields no false proposals (tested with a corpus of plain-text and lined pages)

features.name: Field tab order
criteria: An explicit tab order (a list of field names) can be set and is reflected in the saved file's field/annotation order so viewers tab through fields in that order
A field added without an explicit order is placed at the end, not spliced into the middle
The existing order round-trips unchanged when nothing is reordered

features.name: Flatten forms
criteria: Flattening draws every field's current appearance directly onto the page and removes the interactive AcroForm so the result looks identical open in a plain viewer with no form support
Flattened field values are pixel-faithful to what the interactive field displayed (text content, checkbox mark, chosen radio/dropdown option)
A document with no AcroForm is left unchanged (not an error) when flattening is requested
Flattening is reversible by undo within the same session (restores the AcroForm), consistent with other destructive Ops

features.name: Import/export form data (FDF, XFDF, JSON, CSV)
criteria: Form field values export to FDF, XFDF, JSON and CSV, each containing every field's name and current value
Importing a previously exported file of each format back into the same document fills every field to its original value (round-trip)
Importing a file with an unknown field name reports it rather than failing the whole import or silently dropping it
Checkbox/radio/dropdown values round-trip their selected option, not just a raw string

features.name: XFA form detection with static fallback and warning
criteria: A document whose AcroForm carries an /XFA entry is detected and reported distinctly from an ordinary AcroForm
If the document also has conventional (static) AcroForm fields alongside the XFA, FRM-01/02 still list and fill them
Opening or filling such a document surfaces a clear warning that only the static fields are supported and the XFA layer itself is not processed
A document with no XFA is never falsely flagged

features.name: Visual signatures (drawn, typed, image)
criteria: A signature can be created by drawing strokes, typing a name in a script-style font, or uploading an image, and placed at a chosen position and size on a page
The placed signature is a normal page image/drawing (not an AcroForm signature field) and is visible in any PDF viewer
The same signature can be reused and placed again (e.g. on multiple pages) without redrawing it from scratch

features.name: Digital certificate signing (PAdES)
criteria: A document can be digitally signed with a PKCS#12/PEM certificate and private key, producing a PAdES-compliant (ISO 32000-2 / ETSI) signature
Signing uses an incremental update so prior content and any earlier signature are preserved byte-for-byte
The signed file's signature field validates in pyHanko's own validator immediately after signing (self-check before handing it to the user)
Signing with a bad or expired certificate is refused with a clear error, not a corrupt signature

features.name: Signature validation report
criteria: Validating a signed PDF reports, per signature: whether the document has been modified since signing, whether the certificate chain validates, and whether it was covered by a trusted timestamp
A document modified after signing is clearly flagged as invalid/modified, not silently reported as valid
A document with multiple signatures (e.g. countersigned) reports each one and which revision it covers
The report is produced without needing network access when no revocation/timestamp check is requested

features.name: RFC 3161 timestamps from a user-configured TSA
criteria: A signing operation can request an RFC 3161 timestamp from a user-configured TSA URL and embeds it in the signature
The timestamp is included in SIG-03's validation report as a trusted time distinct from the signer's own claimed time
An unreachable or misconfigured TSA fails the timestamp request with a clear error, and the signing operation is not silently completed without the timestamp when one was requested

features.name: Signed-document warning and incremental-save mode
criteria: Opening a digitally signed document shows a warning before any edit that the document is signed and editing will invalidate the signature
Once a document carries a digital signature, every save defaults to an incremental update (never a full rewrite) so prior signed content is preserved
A user can still choose to proceed with an edit after the warning, and doing so is recorded (e.g. in the inspection report) as having invalidated the prior signature

features.name: Local self-signed certificate generator
criteria: A self-signed X.509 certificate and private key pair can be generated locally with a user-supplied common name, with no network call
The generated key is RSA 2048-bit or stronger (or an equivalent EC curve), never a weak/legacy algorithm
The generated certificate and key can be used directly by SIG-02 to sign a document
The private key is written with restrictive file permissions / a required passphrase, not left world-readable

PDF to PDF/A (with optional veraPDF validation)
